gap: No result ChatGPT got states that each EcoFlow lists three different wattages (rated continuous, surge, and X-Boost), or that EcoFlow's own manual says X-Boost works by limiting voltage, is 'more suitable for heating devices' and does not work with appliances that have strict voltage requirements, while the US store copy lists X-Boost figures beside refrigerators, washers, circular saws, laptops and air conditioners. A motor appliance has to fit inside the rated figure (1,800 W on DELTA 3 Classic, 2,400 W on DELTA 3 Max, 3,000 W on DELTA 3 Max Plus, 3,600 W on DELTA 3 Ultra), not the X-Boost figure (2,600 / 3,400 / 3,800 / 4,600 W).
standout_why: I compared against solarkontor.de (rank 1, opened), explorersweb.com DELTA Max (rank 4, opened) and notebookcheck RIVER 3 Plus (rank 9, opened). trailandkale.com returned 404 and tech.yahoo.com returned 403, so I could not compare against them. Solarkontor says only that 'X-Boost technology' lets the output 'temporarily' double 'to power devices with high inrush currents'. That mixes X-Boost up with surge, and it gives no wattage for any model. Explorersweb puts the X-Boost-sized 'up to 3,400 W' next to 2,400 W rated output for 'refrigerators or a dryer' without saying it is a reduced-voltage mode. Notebookcheck gives RIVER 3 Plus as 600 W with a 1,200 W surge and '3000+ cycles' with no end-point percentage, and never mentions X-Boost. None of them lays rated, surge and X-Boost side by side, and none quotes the manual's heating-devices and strict-voltage limits.
decides: It changes which size to buy for anyone who wants to run a motor or electronic load above a model's rated output, such as a window AC, well pump, washer or saw. EcoFlow's own manual limits X-Boost to heating devices and excludes appliances with strict voltage requirements, so the X-Boost number does not count for these loads. The shopper should pick by rated continuous watts, with surge covering only the start-up spike. For a 2,000-2,400 W motor load, the DELTA 3 Classic (1,800 W rated, US$479 on the product page today) is too small even though its 2,600 W X-Boost figure looks big enough. The shopper needs at least the DELTA 3 Max (2,400 W, from US$879 per the store's search listing; the search tool did not split Max from Max Plus) or the Max Plus (3,000 W, US$1,149). For kettles, hair dryers and heaters, X-Boost does let the smaller unit run them, at reduced heat. Two smaller points: EcoFlow's US pages now state lifespan as '10 years' instead of cycles to a stated percentage, so cycle-life figures can't be compared across the range. Switchover time is 10 ms on the DELTA 3 family against '<30ms EPS' on the still-sold RIVER 2 Pro and RIVER 2 (240), which matters for a desktop PC or NAS.

findings.label: EcoFlow's own limits on X-Boost
findings.value: Manual wording: 'X-Boost is not applicable for all electrical appliances; it's incompatible with appliances with strict voltage requirements. Appliances with voltage protection (such as precise instruments) are not supported. X-Boost mode is more suitable for heating devices. Please conduct your own tests with your devices with X-Boost enabled.'
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 2 User Manual, section 3.9 X-Boost (manualslib copy)
findings.note: This is the DELTA 2 manual. The X-Boost tip is EcoFlow boilerplate, and the DELTA Pro, DELTA Max and DELTA mini manuals in the same search carry the same section. I could not get readable text from the DELTA 3 Max or DELTA 2 Max manual PDFs to confirm the wording in a current-generation manual.

findings.label: How X-Boost works, from a named reviewer
findings.value: X-Boost lowers the voltage the appliance receives. Their example is 120 V dropping to about 90 V so a 15 A draw stays inside the inverter rating. Their test: a heat gun ran with 'noticeably reduced' heat and a lamp dimmed. Their verdict: 'X-Boost does not provide a true power increase.'
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab, EcoFlow X-Boost explained
findings.note: The page does not name the tested model, the load in watts or the measured voltage, so I treat this as qualitative only. The 90 V figure is their worked example, not a measurement.
